title: Runtime routing regret minimizer for attention implementations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement:
We need a pragmatic, production-safe mechanism to pick between multiple attention implementation variants (fused flash attention, blockwise Triton kernels, sparse/windowed attention, and a fallback cuBLAS path) across heterogeneous GPU types and a wide range of sequence lengths. Current static heuristics overfit to single hardware targets and fail for mid-tail traffic (seq_len 128-1024). We want an online system that minimizes latency and cost regret while respecting memory and SLO constraints.

Goals:
- Reduce p95 latency and cost-per-token across mixed workloads by automatically routing to the best attention implementation per request class.
- Maintain safety: no rollout should cause >1% increase in SLO violations or exceed memory budgets.
- Fast warm-start from offline profiles and adapt within minutes to workload shift.

Background/context:
- Our model serving stack supports multiple attention implementations with different trade-offs: low-latency small-seq variants, high-throughput batched kernels for long seq, and memory-conserving sparse options.
- Customers run across A100/H100/RTX-class hardware and both prefill-heavy (large-batch embed/prefill) and decode-heavy (interactive) workloads.
- Existing experiments show that a single static rule (e.g., seq_len threshold = 512) yields 10-25% suboptimal decisions depending on model and hardware.

Proposed approach (four-phase hybrid autotuner):
1) Offline profiling catalog: run targeted microbenchmarks per supported GPU/model-size to build a compact candidate table of latency, memory, and cost estimates for key combos (batch size x seq_len buckets x implementation variant). Store the table as artifact (s3://redwood-artifacts/runtime-profiles/<model>-<arch>-v1).
2) Micro-probing warmstart: on new runtime start or model rollout, run tiny micro-probes (2-10 runs per candidate) on real hardware to calibrate the profile to current driver/software/frequency state. These probes are lightweight and run at low priority.
3) Lightweight sequence-length predictor: infer likely request seq_len distribution from the request metadata and recent telemetry (30m sliding window) to choose the candidate set to evaluate online. This allows prioritizing implementations tuned for expected operating points.
4) Online regret minimizer (constrained bandit): run a low-exploration bandit (Thompson sampling with safety constraints) to route a small fraction of traffic to candidates and update beliefs. Objective: minimize weighted regret = alpha*latency + beta*cost, with hard constraints on memory usage and SLO violation probability. The system should bias exploitation quickly once confidence is reached.

Prefill/Decode scheduling integration:
- Prefill chunking: prefer chunk sizes that keep peak activation memory below a threshold; for very long prefill streams split into 512-token chunks to enable memory-friendly kernels.
- Co-scheduling policy: allow prefill and decode to share GPU when expected latency impact is below delta_ms. When a decode is imminent, prefill can be preempted to avoid user-perceived tail latency jumps.
- Kernel swap cost accounting: include kernel switch overhead (warmup + kernel compile or JIT cost) into the regret objective so the bandit avoids ephemeral switches that harm wall-clock latency.

Success metrics and guardrails:
- Primary: p95 end-to-end decode latency reduction >= 8% vs baseline across mixed traffic in canary.
- Secondary: cost-per-token reduction >= 6% on long-prefill workloads.
- Safety: no >1% absolute increase in SLO violation rate during 24h canary.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 0: lab validation on A100/H100/RTX replicas with synthetic seq_len mixes (Mar 4-8).
- Stage 1: internal canary (5% traffic, non-critical customers) for 24 hours. Monitor p50/p95/cost and memory signals.
- Stage 2: gradual ramp to 25% over 72h if metrics stable.
- Stage 3: full rollout with automatic fallback to static rule after 48h if anomalies detected.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: kernel launch jitter on certain drivers causes noisy estimates. Mitigation: use bootstrapped confidence intervals and require consistent wins over 50 samples before promotion.
- Risk: micro-probing interferes with production. Mitigation: run probes at very low priority and only during low utilization windows.
- Risk: memory under-estimation leads to OOMs. Mitigation: add conservative safety margin and enforce strict per-GPU alloc caps before any routing decision.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implementation completes the offline profiler and micro-prober with correctness tests.
- Bandit routing integrated into runtime and passes canary with defined success metrics.
- Documentation: design doc in Confluence and a short runbook for incident response.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for probe orchestration, cost model math, and constraint enforcement.
- Replay tests driving the online learner with captured request traces (last 14 days) to validate stability.
- End-to-end benchmark comparing p50/p95 and cost across three hardware classes and three seq_len mixes.

2026-03-06 - Miguel: Micro-prober implemented. Observed unexpected kernel launch variance on our A100 testbed with driver 525.15; added a 15% sample noise floor to the estimator. Link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234

2026-03-08 - Design review notes (Ava Chen): Agreed to encode kernel swap cost into the regret function; suggestion to prefer deterministic fallbacks for short interactive traces. Filed follow-up task ENG-80680 for deterministic short-path optimization.

2026-03-09 - Miguel: First internal canary (5% traffic) produced mixed results: p95 down 12% for long-prefill customers, but short interactive p95 regressed 6% on one H100 shard. Investigation points to probe-induced cache fragmentation. Temporarily disabled micro-probes on that shard and re-ran. Dashboard: https://dash.internal.redwood/runtime/eng-80612/canary-2026-03-09

2026-03-10 - Miguel: Added conservative prefill chunking default 512 tokens and co-scheduling tweak to preempt prefill for pending decode within 30ms. Re-ran canary; short-interactive regression resolved. Preparing canary report for PM review.
